title: Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy in High-Risk Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Face: A Prospective Cohort Study
summary:
Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common type of skin cancer. Some tumours have a higher risk of spreading through the lymphatic system to nearby lymph nodes. In other types of skin cancer, examination of the so-called sentinel lymph node is already used to detect such spread at an early stage. This procedure involves removing and examining the first lymph node that cancer cells would be expected to reach if they spread from the primary tumour.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether this procedure may also be useful for patients with a high-risk form of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. The decision whether or not to undergo sentinel lymph node examination is made independently of study participation following consultation with the treating physician. Both groups of patients are subsequently followed for three years as part of routine cancer follow-up. The study will assess whether the cancer returns or spreads and how patients' survival and quality of life develop over time.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Skin of other and unspecified parts of face

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with high-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the face. High-risk features include tumour diameter ≥ 2 cm, tumour thickness > 6 mm, perineural or lymphovascular invasion, poor histological differentiation, invasion beyond the subcutaneous fat, or a high-risk anatomical location involving the ear or lip.
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal to participate in the study or absence of written informed consent.
